A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SegQuant. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial rewriting and repagination.

before.justification: V4 reports original quantization experiments on SD3.5, SDXL, and FLUX, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, activation analyses, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: V5 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds comparator results, layer analyses, and AdaNorm kernel timing measurements.

M1.justification: The core SegLinear/DualScale equations and optimizer/calibrator pipeline remain unchanged. V5 explicitly includes reshape-based multihead merging in Section 4.2.2 and Algorithm 1, whereas v4 lists stack/concat examples non-exhaustively. The PDFs do not establish whether reshape support extends the implemented method or documents existing support.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image quantization on COCO, MJHQ-30K, and DCI using SD3.5, SDXL, and FLUX. ControlNet activation analysis also remains. The added layer benchmarks and removed COCO ablation do not change the overall dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V5 adds Smooth+ (SmoothQuant plus GPTQ) to MJHQ comparisons across all three backbones and introduces PTQ4ViT in the AdaNorm runtime comparison. It adds full-precision reference rows and removes Q-Diffusion from the SD3.5 and SDXL INT8 MJHQ comparisons, while retaining it in other corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: V4 describes evaluation against FP16 outputs, whereas v5 defines FID against real images and reports nonzero full-precision FIDs. Table 4 specifies 32 calibration images versus v4's general 256-image SD3 setting. Figure 10 changes the four-bit efficiency benchmark from W4A8 to W4A4, and Appendix B adds an AdaNorm timing protocol. These are reported protocol changes, not evidence that every experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The existing component analyses receive targeted extensions and removals. V5 removes the COCO component ablation, expands layer-error analysis to SVDQuant and attention outputs in Tables 3 and 10, and adds optimized-layer coverage and automatic segmentation examples in Tables 5 and 11.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Table 1's averaging over 30 diffusion timesteps is retained and is not independent-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: FID values are extensively replaced: Table 2's SD3.5 INT8 SegQuant-G changes from 12.37 to 23.94 under the revised reference, while its other metrics remain unchanged. V5 adds comparator, full-precision, layer, and kernel results; replaces MJHQ ablation values; and removes the COCO ablation and 1.48-times DiT-ControlNet deployment result. Figure 10 changes SegQuant-8 latency from 239.08 to 287.85 ms; its four-bit results use different precision.

T1.justification: V5 removes the explicit DDPM forward-transition and reverse-denoising equations from v4's Preliminaries. The SegLinear/DualScale mathematics and quantization-recovery derivation remain unchanged. The added standard metric formulas are explanatory and introduce no new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The three core contributions and fidelity/generalization claims remain. V5 strengthens their deployment framing by claiming compiler-native static-graph segmentation and hardware-native polarity preservation without custom-operator latency, extending the earlier general compatibility claims.

C2.justification: V5 explains how semantic grouping complements per-channel quantization through shared hyperparameter optimization. It also attributes deployment efficiency to fused BatchedGEMM and selective layer processing, while discussing calibration-search costs and memory bottlenecks. These extend the retained semantic-interference and activation-polarity interpretations.

D1.justification: V5 adds detailed torch.fx tracing, shape propagation, and pattern-detection pseudocode; CUTLASS fusion details; optimized-layer inventories; and FLUX memory-swapping instructions. Appendix B newly reports calibration costs, including approximately 2.5 hours for SD3 and 25 hours with search. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around a Compiler Gap, contrasting SegQuant with manual Q-Diffusion rules and runtime-dependent PTQ4DiT heuristics. V5 adds dedicated video and ViT/SAM positioning, an optimizer/calibrator perspective, and citations including Q-VDiT, DMQ, SpinQuant, and several polarity-aware quantizers. It also newly claims DualScale is the first polarity-aware PTQ scheme designed for diffusion models.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, diffusion background, method motivation, and experimental setup undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. V5 introduces numbered sections and subsections and expands Appendix B into metric explanations, detection procedures, and deployment documentation.

P2.justification: V5 substantially changes the author layout, table-caption placement, comparator/reference rows, and arrangement of displays. It adds four tables and Algorithm 1, expands Figures 8 and 11–13 with reference/Smooth+ panels, revises Figure 9's examples and reference panels, and changes Figure 10's timing axis and precision caption. Figures 14–15 retain their images.

improvement.justification: V5 improves reproducibility and attribution through Algorithm 1, resource disclosures, the matched Smooth+ comparator, and full-precision reference results. These benefits are tempered by the removed COCO component ablation and inconsistent reporting: Section 5.2 quotes FID improving from 15.28 to 12.29, whereas Table 4 reports 23.35 to 22.54 and shows no FID improvement from SEG alone.
